title: A hook cannot tell a child delete that a parent's cascade issues from a hand delete: declare the delete twin of `referentialFieldClear` on the hook context, carried into the QuickJS sandbox
body:
Filing gate ③: a task the maintainer set. objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2078 was ruled letter **C** on 2026-10-13, the maintainer's word verbatim 「hotcrm 三个决裁都同意」, recorded in objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2078 comment `6142043303`. Step 1 of that ruling, quoted: "**The platform half:** the seat files an objectstack card asking for a declared hook-context signal on each child delete that a parent's cascade issues. It is the delete twin of `referentialFieldClear`, carried into the QuickJS sandbox. The named consumers are quote lines and deal lines."
Filed by the `repo:hotcrm` seat (`session_01BCDqr1DqnQjEh5jA9gGkUG`). ⛔ Not a claim. File-at-destination, for triage: `domain:*`, type and grade are the triage seat's.
Reader: the objectstack triage seat routes and grades it; the lane that owns the hook-context contract and the engine's cascade-delete dispatch builds it.
Dedupe (semantic issue search on objectstack-ai/objectstack, all states): "hook context signal for child delete issued by parent cascade delete, beforeDelete cannot tell cascade from hand delete, referentialFieldClear delete twin" → 8 hits; "cascadeDelete hook context key declared isCascade child beforeDelete frozen parent line items" → 6 hits. Nearest: #22305, #20006, #7413, #7477 and #10240, all closed and all about other cascade defects; none asks for this signal.

## The gap

When a record is deleted and its children are removed by the cascade (`deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` on a `master_detail`), the engine deletes each child **as the calling user**. Each child's `beforeDelete` hook then sees the same `ctx.user`, `ctx.session` and `ctx.input` that a user's hand delete of that one child would carry. No declared hook-context key tells the two apart.

- Re-checked on objectstack `origin/main` `107853ce`: `git grep -niE "cascadeDelete|referentialDelete|isCascade|viaCascade" origin/main -- packages/spec/src` finds only the field-level `cascadeDelete` → `deleteBehavior` alias rows (`packages/spec/src/data/authoring-key-lint.ts`). No hook-context key.
- Positive control: the update-side twin exists. `referentialFieldClear` is declared at `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` ~1180–1215: "`true` exactly when THIS write is the engine's own reference cleanup … Absent on every other dispatch". Its docblock gives the reason it had to be declared rather than read off `__referentialFieldClear`: the operation-private key is "the platform's own 'not part of the contract' convention … which is exactly why an app must not build correctness on it", and only a declared key crosses the QuickJS sandbox boundary (`buildSandboxContext` / `installCtx` in `packages/runtime`).

## Who needs it (named consumers, measured)

HotCRM freezes settled records:
- a quote once it is accepted or expired (objectstack-ai/hotcrm PR #2076);
- an opportunity once it is closed (objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2077).

It already refuses a user's line **insert and update** on those. It cannot refuse a user's **hand delete** of one line without also refusing the cascade:
- The HotCRM dev measured a plain delete guard (report on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2060, ablation 2b): a manager deleting **any** accepted or expired quote with lines is refused with the line message, and so is deleting a prospect account that holds one.
- That would break the maintainer's earlier ruling on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#720 (Option A): "A frozen record must not make the people and accounts it references undeletable".
- Sniffing `ctx.transaction` or a `__`-prefixed key to detect the engine's own write is excluded by the ruling recorded on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1165.

Mainstream precedent for the semantics: Salesforce does not fire a child's delete triggers on a master-detail cascade, and Odoo's `ondelete='cascade'` runs in the database without calling the child's `unlink()` guard. A declared signal lets an app keep its guard and yield to the cascade, which is what the update twin already does.

## Ask

1. A declared, read-only hook-context key, `true` exactly on each child delete that the engine's cascade issues while deleting the parent, and absent on every other delete. The name and placement belong to the owning lane; mirroring `referentialFieldClear` is the obvious shape.
2. Carried into the QuickJS sandbox by contract, like `referentialFieldClear`, so that a `*.hook.ts` body can read it.
3. A pin for each face: a cascade child delete carries it; a hand delete of the same child does not; a sandboxed hook body sees it.

## After it ships

objectstack-ai/hotcrm files the consumer card now, `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by:` this card. Once a release carrying the key is installable in HotCRM's pin, that card refuses only a **hand** delete of a settled quote's or a closed deal's line. HotCRM's unlock criterion is "released and installable", not "merged".
